title: Representability in arithmetic: expressing computations

based_on.title: An Introduction to Gödel's Theorems, second edition, corrected Logic Matters reprint

summary: Arithmetic formulas can describe every total computable function, with each particular answer provable from Robinson's seven axioms.
abstract: How much arithmetic is needed to verify a computation? Robinson arithmetic has only seven axioms and no induction schema, yet it can prove the answer to each particular calculation of every total computable function, using one formula to describe that function. For each numerical input it also rules out every other answer. Conversely, a formula with this property gives a computation by searching for proofs. The result connects numerical computation with the strength of a very weak proof system. It supplies separate proofs for individual inputs, without claiming that the system proves termination for all inputs at once.
